title: Ticked, Not Tested, Explained
subtitle: Dagny Okafor, Ingeborg Nwachukwu and Casimir Beng on whether a warehouse's oral food-safety tick predicts what workers still know three months on
summary: A research explainer from the School of Continuous Improvement on Dagny Okafor, Ingeborg Nwachukwu and Casimir Beng's study of the checkbox that closes a warehouse's food-safety refresher. It starts at the oral check itself, a supervisor's two or three questions and the single tick that records them, then sets that tick beside a written retest of nine hundred workers three months on and recordings of the checks themselves. The three authors speak for their own work in turn.
topic: A research explainer of the paper testing whether a warehouse's oral food-safety verification checkbox predicts what workers still know at a three-month written retest, finding the tick a reliable record that the check took place and silent about what it achieved

beats.text: The form does not capture which questions were asked, what the worker said, or how the supervisor judged the answers; the box records only that the conversation happened.

beats.text: Accurate about procedure, silent about substance.
The box was never built to hold an answer. It was built to hold a supervisor’s word that a question got asked, and everyone reading it since has added a promise the form itself never made.
